cultural.vision_reason: This is a red batik cloth with Islamic calligraphy, magic squares, lions, and Dhu'l-Faqar swords — a textile art form (batik is Indonesian craft, plausible for Sundanese/Javanese Muslim communities), not a painting or manuscript.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: This is a calligraphic batik made of cotton. It is dyed red, which is not particularly common, with Arabic calligraphy giving the Islamic Creed combined with protective diagrams (magic number squares, which are popular across SE Asia), powerful animals, in this instance lions, and images of swords representing the double-bladed sword Dhu’l-Faqar given by the Prophet Muhammad to his son-in-law. The lettering between the swords relates to a word of four letters that corresponds to the four numbers found in magic squares, although here it appears that the fourth letter is missing or has been merged with other lettering. Probably produced in Cirebon, west Java, but used in Sumatra.
